findings.problem: fs::read_to_string performs file I/O inside a function that exposes no I/O in its signature or return type. The function signature `load_frames(path: &str) -> Vec<Record>` gives no indication that it performs filesystem reads.
findings.failure_mode: Caller cannot distinguish a missing file from empty input; I/O latency is hidden in a function that appears to be a pure data loader; testing requires real filesystem state.
findings.fix: Remove file I/O from this function. Accept `&str` input text directly (pure parsing) or return `Result<Vec<Record>, IoError>` with an explicit I/O error type. Shell code that reads files should be in a separate action layer.

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics when the file is missing, unreadable, or not valid UTF-8. The absolute laws forbid production unwrap.
findings.failure_mode: Application crashes with panic on any filesystem error instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle gracefully.
findings.fix: Replace with `let text = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))?;` and return `Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>` with a typed error enum.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics when the value field is missing, empty, or not a valid integer. The absolute laws forbid production unwrap.
findings.failure_mode: Application crashes on malformed input data (e.g., a CSV line with a non-numeric value) instead of returning a typed parse error the caller can handle.
findings.fix: Replace with `.map_err(|_| LoadError::Parse(...))?` inside a Result-returning function, using checked parsing with a typed error.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are direct index accesses into a Vec<String> created from split. No bounds check is performed before indexing. Combined with .unwrap() on line 19, any line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields will panic.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV line with fewer than 2 fields causes a panic via index out-of-bounds, instead of returning a typed error.
findings.fix: Use `split_once(',')` to decompose into name and value parts, then return a typed error when the value part is missing. Never use parts[i] without explicit bounds validation.

findings.problem: Raw String and u16/primitive values cross the parse boundary. The `path: &str` parameter is a raw primitive, and `Record` uses `pub name: String` with `pub value: u16` — no domain newtypes, no smart constructor, no validation at the parse boundary. Callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: No enforcement of invariants (e.g., non-empty name, value range) at the type level. Any code that constructs `Record` directly bypasses all validation, making illegal states representable.
findings.fix: Create domain newtypes (e.g., `RecordName`, `RecordValue`) with smart constructors that validate invariants. Use private fields on `Record` with a factory function that returns `Result<Record, RecordError>`.

findings.problem: `parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16` performs a lossy cast from u32 to u16. Any value above 65535 silently truncates. The absolute laws forbid lossy `as` conversions.
findings.failure_mode: Values in range 65536..=4294967295 silently truncate to incorrect u16 values, corrupting data without any indication of data loss.
findings.fix: Replace with `u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| LoadError::Overflow(...))?` to fail explicitly on out-of-range values.

findings.problem: No upper bound on the number of records loaded. No `try_reserve`, no max-items cap, no allocation size limit. The function reads an entire file and collects into an unbounded `Vec<Record>`.
findings.failure_mode: A very large file causes unbounded memory allocation, potentially leading to OOM or denial of service. No allocation budget exists for this data-loading path.
findings.fix: Accept a `max_records: usize` parameter. After parsing the line count or at allocation time, call `records.try_reserve(max_records).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)?`. Return a typed `TooMany` error if the cap is exceeded.

findings.problem: The function fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), logging (println!), CSV parsing, and domain construction (Record creation) into a single 15-line function. This violates the mandatory Data/Calculations/Actions architecture. No separation between shell (I/O) and core (parsing/calculations).
findings.failure_mode: Core parsing logic is inextricably coupled to filesystem access and stdout logging, making it impossible to unit-test the parsing logic in isolation, impossible to swap data sources, and impossible to measure the pure calculation path separately.
findings.fix: Split into: (1) `parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError>` — pure calculation with no I/O; (2) `load_frames(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>` — shell action that reads the file and delegates to parse_record.

findings.problem: `println!("loaded {}", parts[0])` embeds stdout I/O inside a data-loading function. This is a hidden side effect — the function signature declares no I/O behavior. The absolute laws forbid hidden I/O in pure logic.
findings.failure_mode: Function output depends on external state (terminal availability); stdout I/O in hot paths degrades performance; callers cannot suppress logging without modifying the function.
findings.fix: Remove the println entirely from the core path. If logging is needed, pass a logging callback or use a structured logging framework injected from the shell layer.

findings.problem: Uses `line.split(',').map(...).collect()` to materialize all split parts into a Vec<String> when only two fields are needed. The SKILL.md mandates `split_once` for one-separator grammars.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation of intermediate Vec per line. For N lines, this allocates N temporary vectors of potentially many elements. split_once avoids all intermediate allocation and directly decomposes into the two needed parts.
findings.fix: Replace with `let (name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(LoadError::InvalidLine)?;` and parse each part individually.

findings.problem: Record fields are `pub` with no validation. `name: String` accepts empty strings. `value: u16` accepts zero and any value without domain constraints. Public fields bypass encapsulation.
findings.failure_mode: Any code in the crate can construct invalid Record instances (empty names, negative or out-of-range values) without any validation, making illegal states directly representable.
findings.fix: Make fields private. Add a `Record::new(name: String, value: u16) -> Result<Self, RecordError>` constructor that validates invariants. Use domain newtypes for fields that carry rules.

findings.problem: The function allocates a Vec for every line (intermediate split) and a Vec for the final collection. No benchmark, baseline, or profiler evidence exists to justify the allocation strategy. For a frame-loading path, the SKILL.md requires bounded allocation with try_reserve evidence.
findings.failure_mode: Unknown allocation overhead for real-world workloads. The split-into-Vec-then-collect pattern may be orders of magnitude slower than a streaming split_once approach under memory pressure.
findings.fix: Add a benchmark measuring records/sec and bytes allocated. Prove that the allocation strategy is bounded. Use try_reserve with a known max, or stream records via an iterator that avoids Vec allocation.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_frames throughput or allocation
no profiler data showing hot path bottlenecks
no allocation budget or try_reserve evidence
no second-ring evidence for any performance or correctness claim
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate contains 12 Holzman violations including 8 blockers: hidden file I/O, two unwrap panic surfaces, unchecked indexing on split results, a lossy u32-to-u16 cast, unbounded allocation with no try_reserve or max cap, missing parse boundary with raw primitives, fused I/O/parsing/domain logic violating Data/Calculations/Actions separation, and discarded must-use println side effect. The function must be restructured into a pure parse_record calculation and a load_frames shell action, all unwrap calls replaced with typed errors, lossy cast replaced with try_from, split replaced with split_once, and try_reserve with a domain cap added.
